title: Joyalukkas Sets Two Guinness Records With 16.5 kg Gold Jhumkas in Dubai
excerpt: The Indian-origin jewellery group unveiled Mayura Sahasra, a pair of 22-karat gold jhumkas weighing 16.514 kg and measuring 1.215 metres, at its new Jewel of Joy flagship in the Dubai Gold District — now on permanent public display.
body:
• Joyalukkas has entered Guinness World Records with two titles — heaviest pair of gold earrings and largest pair of earrings — for a handcrafted pair of gold jhumkas unveiled in Dubai.
  • The pair, named Mayura Sahasra ("A Thousand Peacocks"), has a net gold weight of 16.514 kg in 22-karat gold — more than five times the previous world record.
  • Fifty-five artisans spent 5,840 hours over several months making the earrings, which measure 1.215 metres long and 0.682 metres in diameter.
  • The earrings are not for sale. They are on permanent public display at Jewel of Joy by Joyalukkas in the Dubai Gold District, open daily with free entry — worth close to $2 million in gold alone at current Dubai prices.

Joyalukkas Jewellery has officially entered the Guinness World Records with two titles — heaviest pair of gold earrings and largest pair of earrings — for a monumental pair of handcrafted gold jhumkas unveiled in Dubai, according to the Press Network of India. The earrings were unveiled by Abdulla Bin Touq Al Marri, Minister of Economy and Tourism of the United Arab Emirates, at Jewel of Joy by Joyalukkas in the Dubai Gold District.

A Thousand Peacocks

Named Mayura Sahasra — "A Thousand Peacocks" — the earrings take their inspiration from the peacock, and every detail of the design echoes its plumage. The jhumkas keep the traditional bell shape of South Asian bridal jewellery, scaled up to 1.215 metres in length and 0.682 metres in diameter. The net gold weight of the combined pair in 22-karat gold is 16.514 kg, more than five times the previous world record. Guinness World Records lists the weight as certified on October 12 in Dubai, ahead of the public unveiling on October 24.

https://x.com/News18Guj/status/2114715443361689844

Fifty-five artisans spent 5,840 hours over several months making the pair by hand. A Guinness adjudicator presented the certificates for both records to group chairman Joy Alukkas and his son John Paul Alukkas, the company's chief executive.

"These earrings are our tribute to this city and to the artisans whose hands turned an impossible idea into gold. Two Guinness World Records titles in one creation is a proud moment for our family."

— Joy Alukkas, Chairman, Joyalukkas

Not for Sale

Joyalukkas said the earrings are not for sale. They will stay on permanent public display at Jewel of Joy, the group's new flagship, which Billionaires Africa reports is open from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. every day with free entry. The company did not put a value on the piece; at a Dubai retail price of about 481 dirhams ($131) a gram for 24-karat gold, the gold in the pair alone would be worth close to $2 million, before any charge for craftsmanship.

A Diaspora Brand's Landmark

Joyalukkas, founded by Joy Alukkas and grown across the Gulf over nearly four decades, dedicated the records to the UAE. John Paul Alukkas said the pair would become a landmark attraction at the store, and described the creation as a complement to Dubai's identity as a city of gold. For the South Asian shoppers who anchor Dubai's gold trade, the display turns a familiar bridal form — the jhumka — into a destination in its own right.
